newsitem.title: BELARUS: World Bank to hold talks in Belarus on new loan.
newsitem.headline: World Bank to hold talks in Belarus on new loan.

text.p: The World Bank is scheduled to hold high-level talks in Belarus next week to look into awarding a new loan if conditions are right, a bank economist told Reuters on Thursday.
"There is very strong evidence that the government has seen the need for market-oriented reforms," John Hansen, senior economist for Europe and Central Asia, said.
"We look forward to working with the government and supporting efforts both in technical assistance and in financial resources," he added.
Hansen gave no exact details of what funding was being considered, but said he was "modestly optimistic" about the chances a deal would be agreed, provided sufficient policies were put in place.
The World Bank halted credits in May until reforms were resumed.
President Alexander Lukashenko keeps a tight rein on economic policy, fixing prices and controlling the central bank.
Hansen said World Bank officials hoped to meet Lukashenko during the visit, due to start on Monday and finish on Wednesday.

Economists are particularly concerned about monetary policy in the former Soviet republic, especially the level of the Belarussian rouble, which was unchanged at 22,380 per dollar on Wednesday in Minsk.
The official rate in Minsk is wildly out of line with the foreign exchange market in Moscow, where the Belarussian unit is quoted at about 29,000 per dollar.
Inflation has picked up sharply in recent weeks, doubling to a monthly rate of 13.3 percent in January.
But new central bank chief Gennady Aleinikov has called for more realistic interest rates and Lukashenko has ordered the government to bring down inflation.
The International Monetary Fund also sent officials to visit Minsk last week but is not considering reopening a $300 million standby credit, most of which was frozen last year.
